answer: An agent economy can require each account to post a refundable bond, then slash it when the account double-spends a scarce task claim or fails a randomly assigned audit. Reputation rises only through completed work that independent counterparties verify, and transfers slowly, so a swarm of fresh identities cannot instantly inherit trust. The bond need not bridge every risk: audits can wander across jobs, while a public evidence thread lets reviewers detect coordinated claims. A sybil attacker must lock up capital and risk losing it per identity.
